lines: Stopped the job, then refused to call it fixed when the job came back. Escalated to the pricing team, and remembered the lesson.

tech.title: Incident injected: Killed job is restarted by its scheduler

events.caption: checkout starts failing (4 timed out so far).

tech.title: Checkout degraded: 4 timeouts since injection, success 0%
12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 91617 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
Checkout success 77% over 10s (7/31 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $4,155/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

detail.query: SELECT s.service, s.slo_success_rate, s.slo_p95_ms, s.verification_window_s, s.revenue_per_minute_cents, s.max_degradation_s, s.tier, t.total, t.failed FROM continuity.service_slo s CROSS JOIN (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN outcome <> 'SUCCESS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed FROM shop.checkout_events WHERE created_at > current_timestamp() - INTERVAL 10 SECONDS) t WHERE s.service = 'checkout'

tech.title: 3 candidate actions enumerated from observed evidence

events.caption: proposes to stop the price sync job.

detail.rationale: The root blocker is pid 91617 running batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction for 4.0s with last statement SELECT 1, blocking 1 session and contributing to 12 sessions waiting on locks [DB-1]. Checkout success is at 55% over 15s [TEL-1] and 77% over 10s vs 95% SLO, with $4,155/min revenue at risk and only 60s tolerance for degradation [BIZ-1]. Memory shows terminating a similar batch_replayable workload (inventory_reconcile) previously restored checkout to 100% [MEM-1]. Need workload registry to confirm replayability and interrupt policy, and tradeoff to quantify cost of interrupt vs wait.

The tradeoff strongly favors termination. All invariants satisfied: workload is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with may_interrupt policy (I1), both workload registry (BIZ-2) and change calendar (BIZ-5) evidence present (I2), no active change-calendar window requiring owner consultation (I3), workload known to registry (I4), waiting EXCEEDS tolerated degradation (I7).
